html:
A 55 km chain of bridges, artificial islands and an undersea tunnel across the mouth of the Pearl River Delta, joining Hong Kong with Zhuhai and Macau. It opened in October 2018, when Xi Jinping attended the ceremony, and is the longest sea crossing in the world.

Three cable-stayed bridges carry the road over the water, and a tunnel of about 6.7 km runs under the shipping lanes between two artificial islands. Building took about nine years and cost several workers' lives.

The bridge cut the trip from Hong Kong to the western side of the delta from hours to under an hour. It was meant to bind the former British and Portuguese colonies to the mainland in a Greater Bay Area of cities. Traffic has been lower than planned, because cars need special permits. Many in Hong Kong saw it as part of the mainland's tightening grip, which came to a head in the protests of 2019.
